paragraphs: Mitzvat aseh liktob parashat "shema" (debarim v, d-t) "vehaya im shema" (sham y, yg-k) uleqabeam al mezuzat happetach diktib "uketabtam veku' lemaan yirbu yemekem veku'" umikkelal hen atta shomea lav veod shehabbayit nishmar bah ukemo sheameru "Adonai shomerek" (tehillim qk, h) adam yashen al mittato bipnim vhqb"h shomero mibbachutz umikkol maqom lo tihyeh kavvanat haadam behannachatah bishbil shemira o sekar olam habba ella leqayyem mitzvat habbore yitbarek vehakkol chayyabin bah gam nashim vaabadim umechannekin haqqetannim laasot mezuza lepitchehen:

clarification.explanation: It is a positive commandment to write the passages "Shema" and "Vehaya Im Shamoa" and affix them to the doorpost, as it is written, "so that your days may be multiplied" — and since Scripture promises a reward (a positive), we also learn of the punishment (a negative) for one who does not fulfill it. Furthermore, the house is protected by the mezuzah, as it is said, "the Lord is your guardian" — a person sleeps in his bed inside while the Holy One guards him from outside. Nevertheless, one should not intend, when affixing the mezuzah, protection or reward in the World to Come, but only the fulfillment of the Creator's commandment. Everyone is obligated in this commandment — men, women, and servants alike, and even minors are trained to affix a mezuzah at their doorways.
takeaways: It is a positive commandment to write the passages Shema and Vehaya Im Shamoa and affix them to the doorpost.
The mezuzah also protects the house, but the intent in affixing it should be only fulfilling the commandment, not protection or reward.
Women, servants, and even minors (for training) are obligated in this commandment.

paragraphs: Im noda lo beshabbat veyom tob sheen mezuza bepitcho veyesh lo bayit acher sheyyesh bo mezuza tzarik sheyyetze mibbayit zeh veyesheb bebayit sheyyesh bo mezuza abal i let leh bayit acher shari ladur sham ad lemachar sheyyetaqqen hammezuza veayyen eshel abraham orach chayyim siman l"ch seip qatan t"v vehu haddin bechol im lo matzuy mezuza yadur belo mezuza ad sheyyimtza ak lo yitatztzel ella yishtaddel bekol maamatztze kocho limtzo veayyen "pitche teshuba" yoreh dea siman rp"h ot ':

clarification.explanation: One who discovers on the Sabbath or a Festival that he has no mezuzah at the doorway, and has another house with a mezuzah — he should leave this house and stay in the house with a mezuzah. But if he has no other house, he may dwell there until the next day to fix the mezuzah. The same law applies on weekdays if no mezuzah is available — one may dwell without one until it is found, but should not be lazy about it, rather should make every effort to find one.
takeaways: No mezuzah at the doorway, with another house having one — move there; no other house — permitted to dwell until the next day.
On weekdays too, if no mezuzah is available, one may dwell until one is found, but should make every effort to find one quickly.

paragraphs: Kesheyyetze mibbeto yannicha yado al hammezuza veyomar Adonai yishmor tzeti uboi lechayyim tobim uleshalom meatta vead olam el shadday yebarek oti veyitten li rachamim:

clarification.explanation: Upon leaving his house, a person should place his hand on the mezuzah and say: "May the Lord guard my going out and coming in for good life and peace, from now and forever; may God Almighty bless me and grant me mercy."
takeaways: It is customary to place a hand on the mezuzah upon leaving the house and say a short prayer for protection and blessing.

paragraphs: Ketzad mitzvat qebiat hammezuza korekah missop happasuq lerosh happasuq veachar sheggolelah mannichah bishpoperet umechabberah bimzuzat happetach bemasmerim o yachpor bimzuzat happetach veyiqbaenna sham velo yamiq lachpor tepach beomeq sheim asa ken pesula diktib al mezuzat velo tok hammezuzot uminhag irenu laasot lah bayit meor gevil kemiddatah vetoperim oto vechotekim meat meor habbayit keneged shem shd"y veen chotekin oto legamre ella nishar sarucha kemo vilon al shem shd"y vezeh haor shel bayit hannizkar yotze mimmennu cheleq meat sarucha mishshene rashin kede sheyyiqbeu sham et hammasmerin bimzuzat happetach umuttar liqboa et hammezuza ballayla deen hepresh bazeh bin layla leyom veayyen leharab "chayyim beyad" yoreh dea siman p"v yeuyyan sham veap al gab deikka tama bazeh keen hattaam sheameru gabbe tzedaqa mishshum deballayla yesh shelita lemazziqin mikkol maqom im nizdammen haddabar kak meelayv lo yachmitz hammitzva:

clarification.explanation: The mezuzah is rolled from the end of the passage to its beginning, placed inside a case (a sheath), and attached to the doorpost with nails, or a groove is carved into the doorpost and it is placed there — but the groove should not be carved a full handbreadth deep, since then the mezuzah would be considered inside the doorpost rather than "on" the doorpost (as Scripture states), rendering it invalid. The local custom is to make a case for the mezuzah from raw animal hide (gevil) sized to it, sew it, and cut a small piece of the hide corresponding to the name "Shaddai" written on the back of the parchment — so that a bit of the hide remains hanging like a curtain, allowing the name "Shaddai" to be visible from outside. The edge of the hide is left with a small protruding flat strip on both sides for affixing the nails. It is permitted to affix a mezuzah even at night — there is no difference between night and day — even though there is a reason for caution (as with charity, since at night there is dominion for harmful forces), if the opportunity arises on its own, the commandment should not be postponed.
takeaways: The mezuzah is rolled from the end of the passage to its beginning, placed in a case, and attached without carving too deep (not a full handbreadth).
It is customary to wrap the mezuzah in hide with an open section through which the name "Shaddai" is visible from outside.
It is permitted to affix a mezuzah even at night.

paragraphs: Kaasher ba leqabea yebarek "asher qiddeshanu bemitzotayv vetzivvanu liqboa mezuza" veachar sheyyiqbaenna yenashsheqenna veyomar "zeh hashshaar laAdonai tzaddiqim yabou bo" (tehillim qych, k) vikavven otiyyot sheniyyot shel hashshaar lah' tzaddiqim hu shem shadday veyomar techilla "leshem yichud qudesha berik hu ushekinetteh veku' hareni meqayyem mitzvat aseh liqboa mezuza kakkatub uketabtam al mezuzot beteka ubishareka vihi noam Adonai elohenu alenu veku'" veyikpol oto shette peamim vehaqqobea mezuzot beshalosh vearbaa petachim yebarek beraka achat lekullan veim hen bishne chatzerot hahalika mibbayit lebayit have hepseq ak hoil veyesh bazeh pelugetta lekak lo yiqbaem semukim ella yishheh ben chatzer lechatzer ezeh shaot veyaaseh hessach haddaat baasaqim acherim benehem kede sheyyebarek bechatzer hashsheni lekulle alema:

clarification.explanation: When affixing the mezuzah, one blesses "who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to affix a mezuzah," and after affixing it, one kisses it and says, "This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it" — intending that certain letters correspond to the name "Shaddai." Before the blessing, one also says a short "for the sake of unification" formula declaring the intent to fulfill the commandment, and afterward "Vihi Noam" (said twice). One who affixes mezuzot at several doorways (three or four) blesses once for all of them, provided they are in the same courtyard; if they are in two separate courtyards, walking between them might be considered an interruption (there is a dispute about this), and therefore it is proper to wait a certain time between courtyards and attend to other matters to create a clear interruption, so he can bless again over the second courtyard according to all opinions.
takeaways: One blesses "to affix a mezuzah" before affixing it, kisses it, and says "this is the gate of the Lord" afterward.
Multiple mezuzot in the same courtyard require one blessing; in separate courtyards, one should wait and attend to other matters between affixings to bless again.

paragraphs: Yiqbaenna beyamin hanniknas veim qebaah bismol pesula apillu bediabad veim yesh shene chadarim semukin zeh lazeh sheyyesh kotel echad mapsiq benehem ubeoto hakkotel yesh petach vehachadarim yesh lahem kol echad petach leatzmo mibbachutz deal ken nimtza petach shebbakkotel haemtzai eno nikkar ezeh mezuza shebbo nechshebet yamin hanniknas kol keha azelinan batar hekker tzir shehacheder asher hatztzirim hem sham nechshab penimi vecheder hashsheni sheen bo tzirim nechshab chitzon veyiqbaenna beyamin hanniknas mecheder sheen bo tzirim lecheder happenimi sheyyesh bo hatztzirim: bammeh debarim amurim kesheyyesh leellu hachadarim petach patucha lekol echad bipne atzmo lechatzer abal im en petach ella raq beechad mehem la azelinan bedin happetach shebbakkotel hammapsiq batar hekker tzir ella leolam anu choshebin leoto hacheder asher happetach qabua bo hu hachitzon vecheder hashsheni penimi veazelinan batar yamin hanniknas mizzeh hacheder shehu chitzon lacheder hashsheni shehu penimi v"p shehatztzirim shel petach shebbakkotel hammapsiq hem nirin bazeh hacheder shehu hachitzon mishshum deen derek likkanes bacheder hashsheni ella raq mecheder zeh hachitzon asher bo happetach patucha lechatzer o lirshut harabbim:

clarification.explanation: The mezuzah is affixed on the right side as one enters the house; if affixed on the left, it is invalid even after the fact. In two adjacent rooms connected by a wall with a doorway (where each room also has a separate doorway to outside), and it is difficult to determine "the right of the enterer" at the doorway in the middle wall — one follows "the recognition of the hinge": the room where the door's hinges are located is considered the inner room, and the other room the outer, and the mezuzah is affixed on the right as one enters from outer to inner. But if only one of the rooms has a doorway to outside (the other has no independent doorway), then the room with the outside doorway is always considered outer, and the other inner, and the mezuzah is affixed on the right as one enters from outer to inner — even if the hinges are actually in the outer room, since the only way to enter the second room is through the outer room.
takeaways: The mezuzah is always affixed on the right as one enters a house/room; affixing on the left is invalid even after the fact.
In adjacent rooms with a shared doorway, which room is "outer" and which "inner" is determined by hinge location or by which room has an independent outside doorway.

paragraphs: Tzerika lihyot zequpa arekkah leorek mezuzat happetach vegam tzarik sheyyihyeh meqom qebiutah al mezuzat yamin hanniknas betok hechalal shel happetach tachat hammashqop ubetepach hassamuk lachutz ubitchillat shelish haelyon shel gobah hashshaar dehaynu techaleq gobah mezuzat habbayit lishlosha chalaqim ubitchillat shelish haelyon millematta lemala shebbo sham tannicha hammezuza veayyen mah shekkatab rabbenu rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar taame hammitzot beparashat vaetchannan yeuyyan sham: veim hinnichah lematta mishshelish haelyon pesula veyesh makshirin bazeh ak en lismok bazeh al hammakshirin ella bedochaq gadol veayyen yad haqqetanna pereq g' seip qatan k"b ayyen sham. abal im hinnichah bashshelish haelyon ella shello netanah bitchillat shelish haelyon millematta lemala ki im hinnichah beemtzao o barosh hannogea bammashqop hare zeh keshera bediabad lekulle alema. meachar sheal kol panim hi munnachat bashshelish haelyon umikkol maqom kol od sheyyukal lahasirah ulehannichah bammaqom harauy lah dehaynu bitchillat shelish haelyon millematta lemala chayyab lahasirah uleqabea karauy veen lismok velomar meachar shekkebar qebaah kak nechshab bediabad vetishshaer bekak ki kevan shebbeemet beyado lahasirah uletaqqenah karauy tzarik laasot ken:

clarification.explanation: The mezuzah must stand upright along the length of the doorpost, and its placement is on the right as one enters, within the doorway's opening, beneath the lintel, in the handbreadth nearest the outside, and at the start of the upper third of the doorway's height (dividing the doorpost's height into three parts, and placing it at the start of the upper third, measured from bottom to top). A mezuzah placed below the upper third is invalid — and although some validate it, one should not rely on this except in great difficulty. If placed within the upper third itself, but not exactly at its start (for example, in its middle or near the lintel) — it is valid after the fact according to all opinions. Nevertheless, as long as the mezuzah can be moved and placed exactly in the proper spot (the start of the upper third), one must do so and not settle for the existing after-the-fact placement.
takeaways: The mezuzah's place: on the right as one enters, in the handbreadth nearest the outside, at the start of the upper third of the doorway's height.
Below the upper third — invalid; within the upper third but not exactly at its start — valid after the fact, though one should still correct it if possible.

paragraphs: Im hinnichah lematta mishshelish haelyon uberak aleha venoda lo achar zeh dela asa yapeh bekak vehesirah kede lehannichah bashshelish haelyon heeleti bsh"q rab pealim bitshuba bs"d dela yebarek aleha atta keshennotelah umannichah karauy vehu chada kevan deikka disbira lah im hinnichah tachat shelish haelyon keshera nimtza ikka bazeh sepeq berakot veqayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel veod apillu lemaen disbira lah pesula epshar lomar demodeh dela yebarek, yaan deniddon didan dame lemah shekkatab maran beshulchan aruk orach chayyim siman q"m seip g'. haola liqrot battora, veheru lo maqom shetztzarik liqrot, uberak al hattora vehitchil liqrot, o lo hitchil liqrot vehizkiruhu shepparasha acheret tzarik liqrot, vegalal hasseper tora lemaqom shetztzarik liqrot bo yesh omerim sheeno tzarik lachazor ulebarek veyesh omerim shetztzarik. vetaam haomerim sheen tzarik lebarek, meporash sham - shekkevan shehasseper tora munnachat lepanayv, vedato aleha liqrot betokah - habberaka kolelet kol happarashiyyot shebbattora veezeh parasha sheyyiqra qae aleha beraka zo shebberek, yeuyyan sham vehu haddin banniddon didan kol mezuzat happetach hi lepanayv beet habberaka veaz chala habberaka gam al shelish haelyon veen lechalleq velomar dezeh tinach im berek uqebaah tachat shelish haelyon vetekep hirgish betauto unetalah uba leqabea bashshelish haelyon dimhanne leh habberaka dedame liqriat hattora hannizkeret abal im hu lo hirgish velo netalah ella achar yom o yomayim veyoter lo tehanne lah habberaka harishona dezeh eno demitzvot mezuza dinah kemitzvat tzitzit deqayma lan lahalaka leinyan berakot kisbara shehebi mvr"m za"l behilkot tzitzit siman Adonai deim pashat tallito shekkebar berak alayv beet shellebasho veatta kesheppashat oto dato lachazor lelabesho miyyad eno tzarik lebarek alayv ki niptar babberaka shebberak alayv bepaam rishona veayyen shulchan aruk lehaggaon rabbenu zalman za"l besiman ch' seip k"g vedin zeh ayre apillu betallit qatan shellebasho uberak alayv veachar arba vechamesh yamim pashat oto lepi shaa addata delachazor ulelabesho degam ken qayma lan deniptar babberaka shebberek alayv keshellebasho paam rishona v"g deyesh pelugta bedin zeh umaran za"l pasaq keman deamar detzarik lebarek shenit mishshum dimtzuvva rishona azela lah vegam habberaka azela lah im kol zeh qayma lan lahalaka kisbara hannizkeret dela yebarek veken haddin bimzuza deim hesirah lepi shaa mishshum ezeh tzorek addata lachazor uleqabea dela yebarek mishshum deniptar babberaka shebberek kesheqqebaah velaken leinyan zeh dehu mesira kede lehannichah bashshelish haelyon gam ken dina haki dela yebarek gam lisbarat happoselin behinnichah tachat shelish haelyon: veod heeleti sham bs"d deim hesirah kede laasot lah tiq acher vechazar uqebaah im lo shaha harbeh lo yebarek veim shaha harbeh shaot baasiyyat hattiq vehalak mimmaqom lemaqom veasa benetayim kamma hessach haddaat baasaqim acherim kol keha yebarek kesheyyabo liqboa otah veayyen admat qodesh cheleq ' siman y" uleshon limmudim siman t' veassedot happisga siman ch' ushear acharonim yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation:
A mezuzah affixed below the upper third of the doorway with a blessing recited, and afterward he learned he had not done it properly and removed it to affix it at the upper third — the Ben Ish Chai wrote in Rav Pe'alim that he should not bless again when affixing it properly, for several reasons: (a) some hold that even below the upper third it is valid, so there is a doubt about blessings — and a doubt about blessings is resolved leniently; (b) even according to those who invalidate it, the first blessing also covers the upper third, following the law of one called to the Torah who blessed and then the scroll was rolled to a different passage, who does not bless again (since the whole scroll is before him and the blessing covers everything) — and here the entire doorpost is before him at the time of the blessing. And one should not distinguish that this helps only if he noticed immediately; since the law of a mezuzah is like that of tzitzit — where one who removed his tallit intending to put it back on does not bless again (the Rema), even after several days; and although Maran ruled that one must bless again, we follow the lenient view not to bless — therefore here too, since he removed it intending to put it back and affix it properly, he should not bless.

Nevertheless, if he removed it in order to make it a new case and put it back: if he did not delay long — he should not bless; but if he delayed many hours making the case, going from place to place and attending to other matters in the meantime (a diversion of attention) — he should bless when he returns to affix it.
takeaways: One who removed a mezuzah (already blessed) to affix it properly at the upper third should not bless again — a doubt about blessings, and the blessing covers the entire doorpost, like tzitzit removed intending to put back on.
Likewise if removed temporarily intending to put it back — no new blessing.
But if delayed long (such as making a new case) with attention diverted to other matters — bless again upon re-affixing.

paragraphs: Ha debaenan sheyyittenenna battepach hassamuk lachutz haynu lekattechilla abal bediabad keshera veim kol zeh im lo hinnichah battepach hassamuk lachutz yesirenna veyannichenna battepach hassamuk lachutz veraq im hu mukrach ledabar zeh lebilti yannichenna battepach hassamuk lachutz hen bishbil shemiratah hen bishbil hekreach acher chashib zeh diabad veshari:

clarification.explanation: The requirement to place the mezuzah in the handbreadth nearest the outside is as the primary practice, but after the fact it is valid even not in that handbreadth. Nevertheless, if not placed there, it should be removed and placed in the handbreadth nearest the outside. Only if there is a necessity not to place it there (for example, for its protection, or another necessity) is this considered after the fact and permitted.
takeaways: The mezuzah should be in the handbreadth nearest the outside as the primary practice, but is valid after the fact elsewhere too; correct it unless there is a necessity not to.

paragraphs: Hinnichah achare haddelet dehaynu shello hinnichah tok hechalal shettachat hammashqop ella hinnichah chutz mehechalal shennimtzet hi achare haddelet hare zeh pesula dederek biatan baenan vekatab harab yd haqqetanna bepereq g' seip qatan y"t deachare haddelet lav davqa ella kol shello hinnichah tok hechalal shettachat hammashqop ben shehinnichah becheleq hammezuza hannimshak veyotze min hechalal shettachat hammashqop lipnim betok habbayit ben shehinnichah bacheleq hannimshak veyotze min hechalal shettachat hammashqop velachutz hare zeh pesula vaapillu im hinnichah samuk mammash lechalal shettachat hammashqop kol sheenah betok hechalal mammash ella chutza lah pesula debaenan derek biateka:

clarification.explanation: A mezuzah placed "behind the door" — that is, not within the doorway's opening beneath the lintel but outside it — is invalid, since it is required that the mezuzah be "in your way of entry" (in the place of actual entry). Rabbi "Yad HaKetanah" clarifies that the intent is not only "behind the door" literally, but any place not within the opening beneath the lintel, whether outside the opening toward the house's interior or toward the outside — even if placed very close to the opening, if not truly within it, it is invalid.
takeaways: The mezuzah must be truly within the doorway's opening beneath the lintel (the way of entry); placement outside the opening, even very close, is invalid.

paragraphs: En happetach chayyab bimzuza ella im ken yesh lo shene mezuzot umashqop vesheyyihyeh chalalah gabohha asara tepachim o yoter velaken bayit sheyyesh lo mezuza mikkan umezuza mikkan vekippa kemin qeshet al shette hammezuzot bimqom hammashqop im yesh begobah hammezuzot asara tepachim beshaveh veyashar beli aqom chayyab bimzuza dahare yesh lo b' mezuzot umashqop veim en bahem eser hattepachim beshaveh veyashar kegon shemmatchil lehitaggel qodem sheyyaggiu laasara tepachim patur mippene sheen lo mashqop vehattaam mippene deal kerichyan tzarik lachshob gam heaqum limzuza deha tzerikin hammezuzot lihyot asara tepachim veen lachshob cheleq min heaqum mezuza vecheleq mimmennu lammashqop vekevan deshadenan lekulleh ammezuza nimtza yesh kan mezuzot belo mashqop veayyen yad haqqetanna seip qatan b':

clarification.explanation: A doorway is obligated in a mezuzah only if it has two doorposts (vertical jambs), a lintel, and an opening height of at least ten handbreadths. Therefore a doorway with two doorposts and a rounded arch (instead of a straight lintel) — if the straight height of the doorposts (before the curve begins) is ten full handbreadths, it is obligated, since it effectively has two doorposts and a lintel; but if the curve begins before reaching ten handbreadths, the doorway is exempt, since one cannot divide the curved section into half-doorpost and half-lintel — the entire curved section must be considered part of the doorpost, in which case there is no lintel at all.
takeaways: A doorway is obligated in a mezuzah only with: two doorposts, a lintel, and a height of at least ten handbreadths.
In an arched doorway, if the curve begins before ten straight handbreadths, the doorway is exempt, since it has no real lintel.

paragraphs: Petach sheen lo ella mezuza achat kegon sheomed beqeren zavit etzel hakkotel shebbazeh nimtza mitztzad echad en bo mezuza dehakkotel ober lehallea min happetach letzad chutz shurat haddin bah hu im hammezuza hahi shel happetach hi mitztzad yamin hare zeh chayyab veim mitztzad semol patur umikkol maqom yiqba bah mezuza belo beraka:

clarification.explanation: A doorway with only one doorpost (for example, standing at a wall's corner, so one side has no doorpost since the wall continues onward) — the basic law is: if the existing doorpost is on the right side, the doorway is obligated; if on the left, exempt. Nevertheless, in either case a mezuzah should be affixed there, but without a blessing (due to the doubt).
takeaways: A doorway with only one doorpost: obligated if the doorpost is on the right, exempt if on the left — but a mezuzah should be affixed in either case, without a blessing.

paragraphs: Bayit sheyyesh bo shelosha ketalim uberucha rebiit en kotel kelal ki happetach memalle kol rucha rebiit middarom latztzapon hare zeh chayyab bimzuza veap al pi sheen lo patztzimin kelal mippene sherashe hakketalim shel tzapon vedarom hen hen patztzimin ki hen atzman chashibi mezuzot:

clarification.explanation: A house with three walls, where the fourth side has no wall at all but the doorway fills the entire side (from south to north) — is obligated in a mezuzah, even though it has no independent "jambs" (doorposts), since the ends of the north and south walls themselves serve as doorposts.
takeaways: A house with a doorway filling an entire side (no wall there) is obligated in a mezuzah, since the adjacent wall-ends serve as doorposts.

paragraphs: Otam hannohagim liqdoach bemaqdeach bimzuzat happetach umannichin sham hammezuza bachor hanniqdach veen nikkar mibbachutz im yesh mezuza la arik lemebad haki ella tzarik laasot siman vehekker al meqom hanniqdach shebbo hammezuza upitche hachatzerot sheppetuchim lirshut harabbim dimzuzat happetach hem binyan abanim umannichim sham hammezuza vetachin besid kol mezuzat happetach kullah yeratza beetzbao et hassid beodo lach keneged hammezuza veyaaseh roshem haretzua bekivvun keneged shem shd"y veday bazeh ki sham i epshar laasot hekker vesiman yoter mishshum haholekim birshut harabbim shello yakkiru sheyyesh sham mezuza veayyen yd haqqetanna seip qatan y"d ubet lechem yeuddeh siman rp"t seip qatan b' yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: The custom of drilling a hole in the doorpost and placing the mezuzah inside it so it is not visible from outside is not proper; rather a distinguishing mark should be made at the drilling site. At courtyard doorways facing a public thoroughfare, where the doorpost is built of stone and plastered with lime — one should scratch with a finger in the wet lime opposite the mezuzah's location, to create a mark corresponding to the name "Shaddai," and this suffices, since it is impossible to make a more prominent mark there without drawing the attention of passersby in the public domain to the fact that a mezuzah is there (with concern of theft).
takeaways: The mezuzah should not be hidden entirely in a hole; an external distinguishing mark should be made.
At courtyard doorways facing the public domain, a discreet mark (a light scratch in the lime) is made, to avoid revealing the mezuzah's location to thieves.

paragraphs: Bemaqom naqi vetahor en rauy lekassot hammezuza abal bemaqom sheyyimmatze bo tinnup lipamim kegon shettinoqot metzuyim sham sheyyetannepu lipamim vekayyotze bazeh tob lekassot hammezuza sheyyasimu keli etz qatan venaqub keneged shem shd"y vesham yannichu chatikot zekukit kede sheyyitraeh hashshem mibbachutz apillu im yizdammen bacheder hahu tinnup lipamim kissuy hazzekukit mehanne lehatztzil "p shennireh hashshem min hazzekukit deqayma lan tzoa baashashit muttar liqrot qeriat shema kenegdah vehu haddin kan dimhanne vehane mille leinyan tzoa vetinnup abal laamod arom keneged hammezuza la mehanne kissuy hashshem bizkukit ella tzarik lehannicha chatikat shaava o dabar acher shello yitraeh hashshem vekol zeh bishbil tzoa vetinnup vesheyyihyeh bemiqreh abal lehannicha tinnup tamid lipne hammezuza en lismok al hakkissuy hazzeh velaken lo yannichu lipne hammezuza tamid keli shel netilat yadayim deshacharit o keli shel me raglayim vetzoa veken lo yirchatzu bigde qetannim shehem meluklakim biri vekayyotze bazeh veayyen yad haqqetanna seip y"g yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: In a clean, pure place there is no need to cover the mezuzah, but in a place likely to become soiled (for example, where infants might soil it), it is good to cover it with a small, perforated wooden container with pieces of glass, so the name "Shaddai" remains visible from outside. Such a covering helps to protect from the impurity of excrement or dirt (similar to the law of "excrement in a glass bottle," where it is permitted to recite the Shema facing it), but does not help for standing naked facing the mezuzah — for that, an opaque item (wax or the like) should be placed to completely hide the name. All this is intended for cases of incidental soiling, but one should not rely on such a covering to permanently leave ongoing dirt near the mezuzah — a hand-washing vessel or vessels with urine/excrement should not be permanently placed there, nor should soiled infant garments be washed there.
takeaways: In a clean place, no covering is needed; in a place prone to soiling, a glass covering protects against incidental dirt but not against standing naked before it.
Ongoing dirt (washing vessels, urine, soiled laundry) should not be permanently left near the mezuzah.

paragraphs: Im yesh mezuza qebua bipnim bacheder shehu betok hacheder kesheyyeshenim bo ish veishto meshammeshin mittatam tzarik keli betok keli vehu sheen hashsheni meyuchad lah deim meyuchad lah apillu mea chashuben keli echad veim munnachat tok qaneh o dabar acher veyesh zekukit al hashshem day biprisat sudar aleha kak katab harab yad haqqetanna seip y"g venahagu haolam lehaqel im mekusseh hashshem kissuy gamur sheeno zekukit kevan shehammezuza geboha asara tepachim min haqqarqa:

clarification.explanation: If the mezuzah is affixed inside a room where a couple sleeps and engages in marital relations, "a vessel within a vessel" is required — that is, a double covering, provided the second covering is not designated specifically for it (since if designated, even a hundred coverings are considered one vessel and do not suffice). If the mezuzah is placed inside a reed or tube with glass over it, it suffices to additionally spread a cloth over it. The common custom is to be lenient with one complete, non-glass covering, since the mezuzah is ten handbreadths above the ground — though height alone does not suffice without a covering.
takeaways: A mezuzah in a couple's bedroom during relations requires a double covering (a vessel within a vessel); the common custom is lenient with one opaque, non-glass covering, since the mezuzah's height alone is insufficient without covering.

paragraphs: Qebaah bimzuzat happetach beod happetach umezuzot shello betalush veaach"k chibberam pesula mippene sheqqadema qebiat hammezuza laasiyyat mezuzat happetach veqayma lan taaseh velo min heasuy vaapillu im haya happetach qabua bakkotel veqaba hammezuza bo kedin vekahalaka veaach"k sateru hakkotel ubanu oto ubaim lehachazir happetach lakkotel vehammezuza odenna qebua bo pesula ella tzarik achar asiyyat happetach bakkotel yesirenna veyachazor veyiqbaenna veayyen mhr" sason siman rl"b uketonet yosep yoreh dea siman g':

clarification.explanation: If the mezuzah was affixed to the doorpost before the doorway and its posts were attached to the wall (that is, while still separate), and only afterward attached — the mezuzah is invalid, since the rule "you shall make it, not from what is already made" requires that the mezuzah's affixing come after the doorway's construction is complete. Even if the doorway was already fixed in the wall and the mezuzah properly affixed, but afterward the wall was demolished and rebuilt and the doorway restored with the mezuzah still on it — it is still invalid, and the mezuzah must be removed and re-affixed after the doorway is built in the new wall.
takeaways: The mezuzah must be placed after the doorway's construction and installation in the wall is complete, not before ("you shall make it, not from what is already made").
Even if the wall was demolished and rebuilt, the mezuzah must be removed and re-affixed after the doorway is restored.

paragraphs: Bayit sheeno meqoreh patur min hammezuza v"g dechatzer chayyab shane chatzer darko bekak lihyot kullo avir veim haya hacheder meqoreh veyesh bo mezuza bepitcho vehesiro aach"k qaruy hacheder vehecheziro oto tzarik littol hammezuza mishsham veyachazor veyiqbaenna achar haqqaruy veap al gab deikka pelugta bazeh sepeqa deorayeta lechumera veyiqbaenna belo beraka beshem umalkut ella yebarek vikavven shem umalko belibbo:

clarification.explanation: An unroofed house is exempt from a mezuzah, unlike a courtyard, which is obligated in a mezuzah even though entirely open to the sky (since that is the normal way of a courtyard). A roofed room that had a mezuzah, and the roofing (roof) was then removed and later restored — the mezuzah must be removed and re-affixed after the roof's restoration, and although this is disputed, a Torah-level doubt is resolved stringently, so it should be re-affixed but without a blessing invoking God's name and sovereignty (only a quiet intention in the heart).
takeaways: An unroofed house is exempt from a mezuzah (unlike a courtyard).
If the roof was removed and restored, the mezuzah must be removed and re-affixed, but without an explicit blessing (out of concern for a Torah-level doubt).

paragraphs: Bayit sheen lo delatot chayyab bimzuza veyesh poterin velaken yiqbaenna belo beraka beshem umalkut o yishtaddel liqboa otah im acherim dechayyabin beraka upoterah bibraka shellahem veharbeh chadarim zeh lipnim mizzeh kullan chayyabin bimzuza veken hu haddin bayit sheyyesh lo petachim harbeh "p sheeno ragil latzet velabo ella raq beechad mehem davqa kullan chayyabin vekol bayit sheen bo d' ammot al d' ammot asher kol amma hi k"d gudalim patur veim yesh bo kede lerabbea d' ammot al d' ammot beshaveh "p shearekko yater al rachebbo o lehepek o shehaya agol o baal chamesh zaviyyot chayyab vecheder qatan sheen bo arbaa ammot al arbaa ammot umishsham niknas lachadarim sheyyesh bahem shiur chayyab liqboa mezuza gam bepetach cheder haqqatan v"g diaka pelugetta bazeh qayma lan sapeq issur tora lehachmir ak yiqbaenna belo beraka veayyen yosep ometz siman t"v veken bayit gadol sheyyesh bo chadarim qetannim lehannicha sham chapatzim chayyabin bimzuza ak lo yebarek veayyen pitche teshuba:

clarification.explanation: A house without doors is obligated in a mezuzah, even though some exempt it — therefore a mezuzah should be affixed but without a blessing, or one should try to affix it together with other doors certainly obligated, to be covered by their blessing. Many rooms one inside another are all obligated in a mezuzah; likewise a house with many doorways, even if only one is actually used for entering and exiting, all are obligated. A house lacking four cubits by four cubits (each cubit about 24 fingerbreadths) is exempt, but if it can be squared to four by four (even if its shape is not square — a rectangle, circle, pentagon) it is obligated. A small room (below this measure) through which one enters larger, obligated rooms — is itself also obligated in a mezuzah at its doorway, but without a blessing (due to the dispute). Likewise a large house with small storage rooms is obligated in a mezuzah without a blessing.
takeaways: A house without doors is obligated in a mezuzah without a blessing (or one tries to join it to another doorway with a blessing).
A small room below the minimum measure (4x4 cubits) is exempt, but if it serves as a passage to a larger obligated room, a mezuzah is affixed there without a blessing.

paragraphs: Otzerot yayin veshemen vekayyotze veken bet hatteben bet haetzim ubet habbaqar sheen bo meus chayyabin, kevan deyotzein veniknasin bo umishtammeshin sham chashib bet dira vecheder shehannashim rochatzin bo kevan sheameddam sham arumot en kebod shamayim lihyot sham mezuza abal im yesh bo delet vedarkan lisgor haddelet beet rechitza da hammezuza mibbachutz chayyab bimzuza ubet hakkisse ubet hammerchatz ubet habburseqi ubet hattebila peturim lepi sheen asuyin ledirat kabod:

clarification.explanation: Storerooms for wine, oil, and the like, and storerooms for straw, wood, and cattle that carry no repulsiveness — are obligated in a mezuzah, since people enter and exit and use them, and they are considered a dwelling. A room where women bathe while naked — there is no honor of Heaven in affixing a mezuzah there; but if there is a door customarily closed during bathing, and the mezuzah is placed outside the door, it is obligated. An outhouse, a bathhouse, a tannery, and a mikveh building are exempt, since they are not made for a respectable dwelling.
takeaways: Storerooms for wine/oil/straw/wood/cattle are obligated in a mezuzah like an ordinary dwelling; a women's bathing room — the mezuzah goes outside the closed door.
An outhouse, bathhouse, tannery, and mikveh building are exempt, since they are not a respectable dwelling.

paragraphs: Bet shaar sheppatucha lashshaar velechatzer chayyab bishte mezuzot achat bemaqom sheppatucha labbayit veachat bemaqom sheppatucha lechatzer veken bet shaar haomed ben hagginna labbayit chayyab bishte mezuzot kannizkar. ubet hakkeneset im yesh sham bet dira leshum adam chayyab veshaare chatzerot happetuchim lirshut harabbim, im yesh lachush sheyyignebu haggoyim hammezuza veyabou kitbe haqqodesh lide bizzayon vei epshar leshameram peturim:

clarification.explanation: A gatehouse open both to the street and to a courtyard is obligated in two mezuzot — one at the opening to the house and one at the opening to the courtyard; the same applies to a gatehouse standing between a garden and a house. A synagogue, if it also contains a dwelling for a person, is obligated in a mezuzah. Courtyard gates open to the public domain — if there is concern gentiles might steal the mezuzah, leading to the desecration of sacred writings, and it is impossible to guard them, they are exempt.
takeaways: A gatehouse with two openings (to the street and to the courtyard) is obligated in two mezuzot.
Courtyard gates open to the public domain, with real concern of mezuzah theft and desecration that cannot be prevented, are exempt from the commandment.

paragraphs: Chanuyot shel sechora sheyyoshebin bahem socharim kol hashshana kullah "p sheen yoshebim ella bayyom ki ballayla holekim lebattehem hare ellu chayyabin bimzuza veayyen yad haqqetanna, mihu yannicha belo beraka ki ht"z za"l choleq bazeh upoh irenu yesh pundaqim kaanaat (mibtzere "chan", shoq namel sitonaim limlunot,yammaim vesochare chutz) meleim chanuyot sheyyoshebim bahem hassocharim kol hashshana kullah venahagu shello lehannicha sham mezuza vehattaam ki bepundaq yesh bo chanuyot sheyyoshebim sham goyim vesameku bazeh al mah shekkatab rama" za"l besiman rp"v seip ' gabbe chatzerot shemmiqtzat goyim darim sham dipturin:

clarification.explanation: Commercial shops where merchants sit all year (even if they return home only for day and night) are obligated in a mezuzah, but it should be affixed without a blessing due to a dispute (the Taz disagrees on this). In Baghdad there are khans (trading inns) full of shops where merchants sit all year, and the custom was not to affix a mezuzah there at all, since gentiles also reside in these inns, relying on the halacha exempting courtyards where gentiles also dwell.
takeaways: Permanent commercial shops are obligated in a mezuzah, but without a blessing (a dispute).
In Baghdad, no mezuzah was affixed in the khans, since gentiles also resided/sat there.

paragraphs: Hassoker bayit beeretz yisrael chayyab bammezuza miyyad mishshum yishshub eretz yisrael abal hassoker bayit bechutza laaretz vehaddar bepuneddaq beeretz yisrael patur mimmezuza sheloshim yom bammeh debarim amurim? besoker bistam, abal im sakar beperush leshishsha chodashim o leshana meachar shessakar beperush lizman shehu yoter mishsheloshim veqana sekirut habbayit beopen sheen echad mehem yakol lachazor bo veholik sham kelayv umittaltelayv hare zeh mitchayyeb miyyad v"g deharab chiqre leb beyoreh dea cheleq g' siman qk"ch sebira lah deachar sheloshim yesirenna veyachazor veyiqbaenna anachnu morin deen tzarik lahasirah achar sheloshim uleqabea mechadash vekaasher hora beyosep ometz siman l' lehaggaon or hachayyim:

clarification.explanation: One who rents a house in the Land of Israel is obligated in a mezuzah immediately, due to the importance of settling the Land; but one who rents a house outside the Land, and likewise one dwelling in an inn in the Land of Israel, is exempt from a mezuzah for the first thirty days. This is true for an ordinary rental, but if he rented explicitly for a long period (half a year or a year), in a manner where neither party can retract, and brought his belongings in — he is obligated in a mezuzah immediately. There is a dissenting view holding that the mezuzah should be removed after thirty days and re-affixed, but Rabbi Yosef Chaim rules this is unnecessary.
takeaways: One renting a house in the Land of Israel is obligated in a mezuzah immediately; outside the Land (or an inn in the Land of Israel) is exempt for the first thirty days in an ordinary rental.
An explicit long-term rental (half a year/a year) with belongings brought in immediately requires a mezuzah immediately, with no need to remove and re-affix after thirty days.
